root.label: Strict aliasing and UB
root.note: UB is an assumption the optimizer may make; the aliasing rule is one of the assumptions it relies on most.

children.label: Abstract machine
children.note: Implementations only need to reproduce the observable behavior of the abstract machine.

children.label: No requirements
children.note: An execution containing UB has no requirements, even for operations before the UB.

children.label: Optimizer assumptions
children.note: Null checks after a dereference and x + 1 > x on signed int can be folded away.

children.label: Behavior categories
children.note: Four distinct kinds of non-portable behavior.

children.label: Implementation-defined
children.note: One behavior, documented by the implementation, such as sizeof(int).

children.label: Unspecified
children.note: One of several allowed outcomes, undocumented, such as function argument evaluation order.

children.label: Ill-formed NDR
children.note: The program is invalid but needs no diagnostic, such as an ODR violation.

children.label: Erroneous behavior
children.note: C++26 only: uninitialized reads give an implementation value, with [[indeterminate]] to opt out.

children.label: Type-accessibility rule
children.note: [basic.lval] restricts which glvalue types may access an object's stored value.

children.label: Allowed types
children.note: The dynamic type (up to cv), its signed or unsigned counterpart, and char, unsigned char, std::byte.

children.label: signed char excluded
children.note: Unlike C, C++ does not let signed char access arbitrary objects.

children.label: One-way exemption
children.note: Bytes may view any object, but a byte buffer cannot be read as an int that is not there.

children.label: Punning
children.note: Reinterpreting bytes as another type needs a sanctioned tool.

children.label: Union punning is UB
children.note: Only the active member is alive; C defines punning, and GCC allows it at run time as an extension.

children.label: memcpy and bit_cast
children.note: memcpy copies representations; bit_cast (C++20) needs equal size and trivially copyable types.

children.label: start_lifetime_as
children.note: C++23: makes an implicit-lifetime T from bytes already in place, with no copy.

children.label: Pointer provenance
children.note: A pointer points to a specific object; its arithmetic and casts depend on that object.

children.label: Array bounds
children.note: Arithmetic stays within the array or one past the end; forming any other pointer is UB.

children.label: Pointer-interconvertible
children.note: Only union and member, or standard-layout object and first member, retarget via reinterpret_cast.

children.label: Unrelated comparison
children.note: Built-in < on unrelated pointers is unspecified; std::less gives a total order.

children.label: Constant evaluation
children.note: Core-language UB makes an expression non-constant, so it must be diagnosed.

children.label: constexpr as UB checker
children.note: A static_assert over a constexpr test turns overflow, bad reads and bounds errors into compile errors.

children.label: Limits
children.note: Library-precondition UB need not be diagnosed, and compilers have gaps.
